title: probabilistic-noise-attribution-and-decision-tree-executor-for-oncall
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a probabilistic attribution layer and decision-tree executor that reduces noisy pages by grouping signals across regions and subsystems, attributing them to likely root causes, and automatically executing safe, reversible playflows (suppress/annotate/escalate/failover). This integrates with SLO metadata, circuit-breaker state, and load-shedding policies so decisions respect availability targets and minimize blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype attribution ML model returns top-2 root-cause candidates with confidence scores for injected multi-region alert storms
Decision-tree executor can run three safe playflows: annotate-only suppression, scoped failover to secondary region, and controlled load-shed while preserving primary SLOs
Oncall UI cards show attribution, confidence, and recommended action; one-click approve executes the automated playflow
Automated actions are fully auditable in the incident timeline and reversible via a single revert operation
System respects per-customer and per-route SLOs and tenant isolation (no cross-tenant failovers)
work_items: instrument cross-region alert aggregation stream (kinesis->materialized view)
train lightweight Bayesian attribution model on historical incidents (use features: time-windowed counts, error-types, latency skew, topology tags)
design decision graph DSL and implement safe primitives (annotate, suppress, route-shift, shed, rollback)
integrate with circuit-breaker service to read/modify state and with autoscaler for scoped capacity adjustments
UI: oncall card + confirm modal + revert action
add observability: audit log, pre/post SLO delta estimation, and a canary test harness
